body.x: PABLO AIR (CEO Youngjoon Kim) participated in CES 2025, held from January 7 to 10 (local time) in Las Vegas. The company showcased its advanced drone technologies at the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion.

Known as a leading Korean startup in drone innovation, PABLO AIR specializes in autonomous swarm control technology and integrated mobility management platforms. The company’s core technology enables the integration and control of multiple unmanned vehicles using diverse communication protocols within a unified system, allowing real-time information sharing and collaborative execution of complex missions.

PABLO AIR has expanded its operations to include defense technology, drone art shows, drone delivery, and UAM (Urban Air Mobility) traffic management platforms, making it a versatile player in the mobility sector.

At CES 2025, PABLO AIR unveiled its ‘PabloX’ lineup and the newly developed ‘PabloX F40,’ the world’s first multipurpose drone with an integrated pyrotechnic system. The drone’s innovative design significantly reduces technical errors associated with additional equipment attachments, enhancing operational efficiency.

The company also introduced the ‘PabloX Smart CLS’ system, designed to revolutionize drone art shows by enabling simultaneous charging, transportation, and storage of multiple performance drones. This system significantly reduces operational costs and manpower requirements, providing a sustainable and efficient entertainment solution.

body.cap: Interview with PABLO AIR CEO Youngjoon Kim and AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Additionally, PABLO AIR demonstrated its UAM traffic management platform, UrbanLinkX, which was previously selected as the CES 2023 Innovation Award Honoree. This interactive display allowed visitors to experience future mobility scenarios firsthand, further solidifying the company’s reputation for cutting-edge unmanned vehicle control technologies.

A PABLO AIR representative stated, "As a leading tech company from Incheon, PABLO AIR is here to promote our unique and innovative performance drone lineup, including the PabloX series. We aim to expand partnerships and boost sales for drone shows and hardware. These drones are developed with 100% Korean technology and boast world-class quality and competitiveness."

The representative added, "Following the successful debut of PabloX F40 at last year’s CES, which marked our first export milestone, we are excited to introduce the PabloX Smart CLS system. This new solution simplifies large-scale drone logistics and setup, positioning us as a key player in the global drone market. With approvals from U.S. regulators and growing interest from Asia and the Middle East, we anticipate that CES 2025 will accelerate our brand’s growth and influence."
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
